notes: Only HVS7 and HE 0437-5439 are named stars tied to the paper’s HVS discussion; because the paper treats them as previously known HVSs rather than selecting new individual unbound candidates, both are follow_up. HVS7 is explicitly linked to a relaxed 900 km s−1 HVS threshold at T:p5-b4. HE 0437-5439 is discussed as an HVS that could be a BHB at T:p7-b2. The Galactic-centre S-stars S2 (S0-2) and S14 (S0-16) at T:p4-b6 and T:p5-b4 are orbital benchmarks, not Galactic-unbound candidates, and Sgr A* (e.g., T:p1-b5) is the central SMBH; these are excluded. Other observed HVSs are treated only as an unnamed population (e.g., T:p1-b8), so no further individual identifiers can be recorded.

HVS7: The target identifier HVS7 appears only once in the paper (T:p5-b4): "If we relax our definition of a HVS and set v_ej = 900 km s^-1, the ejection velocity of HVS7 (Carlberg & Innanen 1987; Brown et al. 2006b), we get ~50 HVSs." This is a selection threshold adopted from prior work (the ejection velocity used to classify HVSs), not a measurement of HVS7's present-day position, distance, parallax, proper motion, or line-of-sight velocity; no tabulated quantities for HVS7 are given anywhere in the text, tables, or figures. Consequently no eligible quantities are reported for HVS7.

HE 0437-5439: The paper is a theoretical study of hypervelocity star production via scattering off stellar-mass black holes near Sgr A*. The target star HE 0437-5439 appears only once, in the discussion (T:p7-b2), where the authors argue that it "should not be ruled out as being a BHB star based on its required spin value alone." No position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, or other quantity for HE 0437-5439 is reported in the supplied material, so no quantities can be extracted.
